action: Issue an urgent public policy statement on the RoboRide expansion announcement. The statement has three specific components: (1) Welcome the price reduction as a sign the competitive framework is working, but make clear that lower prices do not reduce the company's obligations under the municipal operating license — the workforce fund fee applies to every ride, including at $0.12/mile. (2) Issue a formal notice that the delivery partnership announced today is not covered under the existing operating license, which was issued for passenger transportation services only. RoboRide must apply for a delivery operations amendment to the license within 30 days or cease delivery operations in Millfield. The amendment application will carry the same workforce fund fee structure and local hiring preference clause. (3) Announce an emergency task force session within 10 days to review whether the licensing framework needs to be updated to address residential coverage expansion and multi-service operations. I am not slowing them down. I am making sure every new service line is covered. This statement goes out the same day as their announcement. I do not give them 72 hours to establish the consumer-benefit narrative unchallenged. The council press contact sends it to local news and I post it publicly. This is the policy action this tick.
